en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sappāṇakavagga 66.
The Training Rule on Robbery Caravans.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain caravan was about to set out from Rājagaha for Paṭiyālaka.
A certain bhikkhu said to those people,
"I too will go along with you, venerable sirs."
“Venerable sir, we shall avoid paying the toll.
“Understand for yourselves, friends,” he said.
Then the laborers heard:
“The caravan, it seems, will evade the toll,” they said.
They then blocked the road.
Then those toll-collectors seized that caravan, cut off [the way], and said this to that bhikkhu:
“Venerable sir, why do you knowingly travel with a band of thieves?
Having bound him, they released him.
Then that bhikkhu went to Sāvatthī and reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so forth]... were indignant, disparaged, and complained, saying:
"How can a monk, knowing it to be so, travel along a highway in company with a band of thieves?
... [and so forth] ... "Is it true, monk, that you, knowing it to be so, traveled along a highway in company with a band of thieves?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“… How can you, foolish man, knowingly set out on a journey together with a caravan of thieves? This is not for one who seeks to train.”
“Monk, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
[and so forth] ...And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

‘If any monk, knowing that he is traveling with a band of thieves, should set out on the same road with them, even if only as far as the next village, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whoever" means whoever of such a kind...
"a monk."
...pe... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Knows" means he knows it himself, or others inform him of it, or he informs [others] himself.
"A caravan of thieves" means either robbers who have already committed their deed or those who have not yet committed it; they either go to steal from a king or evade customs duties.
"Together with" means...
"From one side.
"Having made an appointment" means:

if one makes an appointment, saying, "Let us go, friend," "Let us go, venerable sir"; or "Let us go, venerable sir," "Let us go, friend"; or "Today, or yesterday, or tomorrow, let us go"—there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"Even as far as the interval between villages" means:
in a village where a cock can fly from one house to another, for every interval between such villages, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
In a forest where no village exists, for every half-yojana, there is an offense of expiation.

If one travels along a highway with a caravan of thieves, perceiving it to be a caravan of thieves, having made an appointment, even for as little as the distance between two villages, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If one travels along a highway with a caravan of thieves, being doubtful about it, having made an appointment, even for as little as the distance between two villages, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).

If one travels along a highway with a caravan of thieves, perceiving it to be not a caravan of thieves, having made an appointment, even for as little as the distance between two villages, there is no offense.
If the bhikkhu makes arrangements, but the people do not, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is a caravan of thieves and he perceives it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is a caravan of thieves and he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if it is a caravan that does not carry goods and one perceives it as such.
There is no offense if one goes without having made an appointment.
People have made an appointment, but the bhikkhu has not;
he goes at a different time, or there is an emergency.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The sixth training rule concerning traveling with a caravan by theft is finished.
